summary: In a source restyle the deck's header contract governs only the pages whose own source carries header furniture: a running header block or that page's number. Front and back matter are exempt.
invariants: The exemption is derived from the pinned manifest alone, so it is identical on every attempt and every replay.
A page is exempt only when it carries neither a block repeated on at least half the deck's pages nor its own page number.
Exempt slides receive no header contract at all: no band brief, no requirement slot, no chapter breadcrumb, and no header validation.
Every other slide still reproduces the deck's one header design exactly.
Decks with no source content (ordinary authored generation, page remake, quality review) keep an empty exemption set and are unchanged.
Whether a restyled deck prints page numbers follows the source manifest, not the header-contract call: a source that numbers its own pages is always authored in template page-number mode.
forbidden: Require a header band on a page whose source has none.
Derive the exemption from the authored HTML rather than from the source manifest.
rationale: Operation ce48036c spent both of slide 35's provider calls, and then the deck, on header_band_missing: the source closing page is a logo, a statement, a subtitle and a footer, with no running header and no page number, so the model composed it full-bleed and the contract rejected a faithful composition.
Role exclusion already existed for COVER and SECTION but is positional and keyword-derived, which cannot see that a particular source page has no header.
Measured on the real 35-page deck: exactly pages 1 and 35 are exempt, and all 33 content pages carry both the running header and their number.

The contract call judges a deck's design from a content sample and answered pageNumbers=False on the same 35-page source it had answered True for; that run instructed every slide to render no page number and no footer text, and then failed 8 slides for the missing source text.
